transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Lately I can’t seem to focus on my analyses at work—my mind keeps going blank even when I’m staring right at the spreadsheets. I'm a management analyst, and it's getting really difficult to do my job when I just freeze up like that.
Did these concentration problems start after a specific stressful event or change in your life, or have they been building up gradually without one clear trigger?

It really started after I got promoted to a much higher-visibility role about fifteen months ago. While that promotion was the initial trigger, the concentration difficulties and the pressure have gradually built up and gotten much worse over the past year as the workload escalated.
Have these symptoms been present most days for at least 6 months, even when you are not dealing with a specific work stressor, or do they mainly come and go in response to the stressful situation?

Yes, they've been present almost every single day for about fifteen months now, ever since I started the new role. It doesn't just come and go; even on weekends or during trips, the anxiety is constantly there and I can't seem to relax.
Do you also have physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, fatigue, irritability, or trouble sleeping along with the anxiety?

Yes, definitely. Most nights I lie awake until 2 or 3 a.m. replaying work scenarios in my head, and even when I do sleep, I wake up constantly and feel completely unrefreshed. I'm also exhausted all the time—even on weekends, it feels like I'm dragging my body through molasses before I even start my day.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different things, not just work, and is the worry hard to control even when you know it may be excessive?

Yes, my mind is constantly spinning about everything, from work mistakes to minor things like whether I remembered to lock my apartment door. It feels completely uncontrollable; even when I try to distract myself with a book or a show, the "what if" thoughts quickly sneak back in and snowball into worst-case scenarios.
Do you ever have sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like you might lose control?

No, I don't experience those sudden, intense panic attacks or things like a racing heart or shortness of breath. My anxiety is more of a constant, non-stop mental worry and tension that just lingers all day long rather than hitting me in sudden spikes.
Do you ever avoid situations or places because you worry they might trigger your anxiety, or do you mostly feel anxious even when you are not in any particular situation?

The anxiety is constant and always running in the background of my mind, no matter where I am or what I'm doing. I don't avoid specific places or triggers, but I have started turning down social plans with friends. That's just because I feel too wired, overwhelmed, and behind on work to actually show up and enjoy myself.
Over the past 15 months, have you also felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I have definitely lost the ability to enjoy things I used to love, like going on trips, seeing friends, or going for runs with my running club. It's not really that I feel depressed or hopeless in a traditional sense, but rather that I'm just too anxious, wired, and constantly consumed by work worries to actually show up and enjoy myself.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most days, or lost interest or pleasure in things nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down, depressed, or hopeless; it's more that I feel extremely anxious, tense, and overwhelmed. While I have stopped doing things I used to enjoy like running or seeing my friends, it is because I feel too anxious and behind on work, rather than feeling depressed.
Do you find it very hard to control the worry, and does it feel excessive compared with the actual situation most of the time?

Yes, it feels completely uncontrollable and highly excessive. Even if I try to distract myself with a show or a book, the "what if" thoughts quickly sneak back in and snowball into worst-case scenarios. I'll spend hours obsessing over whether a tiny typo in a presentation is going to ruin a client relationship or get me put on a performance plan.
Did your anxiety begin within 3 months of the stressful promotion, or did it continue for much longer than that after the stress started?

Yes, the anxiety and tension started almost immediately after I stepped into the new role fifteen months ago, definitely within those first few weeks. It has continued steadily and hasn't let up at all since then.
Has your anxiety ever been present for 6 months or more without being tied to a specific stressor, or did it start and stay closely linked to the promotion and work changes?

It started with the promotion about fifteen months ago and has been constant since then, so it has definitely been present for over six months. While it was initially triggered by and remains heavily focused on my work demands, it has now expanded to non-work things as well, like constantly worrying about whether I locked my apartment door.
Did your symptoms start within 3 months of the promotion and stay closely tied to that stressor, or did they continue as a more general anxiety problem even after you adjusted to the new role?

They definitely started within those first three months of the promotion, but I never really adjusted and they didn't go away. Instead, the anxiety has snowballed into a constant, general problem that affects almost every area of my life, even causing me to worry about everyday things like whether I locked my apartment door.
Have you ever had a period of at least 6 months before this promotion when you were also a chronic worrier about many different things, or is this the first time you’ve had anxiety like this?

This is definitely the first time I’ve ever experienced anxiety and worrying to this extreme degree. Before my promotion, I was always highly organized and used meticulous planning to manage stress, but I never had this kind of chronic, uncontrollable worry. These severe symptoms only started and became constant after I stepped into this new, high-pressure role.

Before this promotion, did you ever have a period of at least 6 months where you were worried about many different things most days and found it hard to control the worry? Or is this the first time you’ve had this kind of ongoing anxiety?

This is definitely the first time I've ever experienced this kind of ongoing, uncontrollable anxiety. Before the promotion, I was always a meticulous planner and handled my responsibilities well, but I never had this constant, overwhelming worry. This level of tension only started after I took on the new role about fifteen months ago.
Do you feel your anxiety is mainly a response to the work promotion and its demands, or would you still have the same level of worry even if that stressor were removed?

While the promotion definitely triggered this, the anxiety now feels like it has taken on a life of its own. Even if you removed the work stress entirely, I think my brain would still find things to worry and spin out of control about. It has already spread to non-work things like obsessing over whether I locked my apartment door or being completely unable to relax on weekends.
Did your symptoms start only after the promotion and seem directly tied to that stress, or did you already have this kind of constant worry before the promotion?

No, I never had this kind of constant worry before the promotion; it only started after I took on the new role about fifteen months ago. While I've always been a meticulous planner, this overwhelming, uncontrollable anxiety and inability to relax only became an issue once I stepped into this high-visibility position.
If the work promotion and job pressure were removed, do you think your anxiety would mostly go away, or would you still have the same level of worry most days?

While the promotion definitely triggered this, I feel like the anxiety has taken on a life of its own now. Even when I try to step away by watching a show or going on trips, uncontrollable 'what-if' thoughts hijack my mind and make me worry about non-work things, like whether I locked my apartment door. I suspect that even if the work pressure were completely removed, the worry would just find something else to latch onto.
If the work promotion and pressure were completely removed, do you think your anxiety would mostly go away, or would you still have the same constant worry most days?

I honestly think the constant worry would still be there. It feels like the anxiety has taken on a life of its own now, and even if work was fine, my mind would just find other things to obsess over, like whether I locked my apartment door. I just can't seem to turn off this constant tension anymore.

Before this promotion, did you ever have a period of at least 6 months where you were worried about many different things most days and found it hard to control the worry? Or is this the first time you’ve had this kind of ongoing anxiety?

This is definitely the first time I’ve ever experienced this kind of ongoing, uncontrollable anxiety. Before my promotion about fifteen months ago, I was always able to manage my work and life well using planning and calendar-blocking. This severe, constant worry only became my normal after stepping into the new role.
Do you feel your anxiety is mainly tied to the work promotion and its demands, or would you still have the same level of worry most days even if that stressor were gone?

Although the promotion and its intense demands definitely triggered this spiral, the worry has now spread to minor daily things like constantly worrying if I locked my apartment door. Because my mind is always spinning, I honestly don't think it would completely go away even if the work stress were removed. It really feels like the anxiety has taken on a life of its own now.
Did your symptoms start within 3 months of the promotion and stay mainly tied to that stressor, or did they continue as a broader, ongoing worry problem even after you had time to adjust?

Yes, they started within those first few weeks of the promotion, but instead of fading as I adjusted, the worry just snowballed into a constant, uncontrollable pattern. It has expanded far beyond work tasks to broader, everyday concerns—like constantly worrying if I locked my apartment door—and it hasn't let up at all since then.
If the work promotion and job pressure were completely removed, do you think your anxiety would mostly go away, or would you still have the same constant worry most days?

I really think the worry would still be there because the anxiety has taken over my whole brain now. It has expanded to everyday things, like constantly second-guessing if I locked my apartment door. I feel so constantly wired that I doubt it would just completely disappear even if the job pressure was gone.
Do you think your anxiety would mostly go away if the promotion and work pressure were removed, or would you still have the same constant worry and tension most days?

Even if the work pressure were completely removed, I believe the worry would persist because it has taken on a life of its own now. I find myself constantly stressing over non-work things, like whether I locked my apartment door, and I just can't seem to turn off the "what-if" thoughts. This constant state of tension has become my new normal, and I don't think it would simply go away.

Before this promotion, did you ever have a period of at least 6 months where you worried about many different things most days and found it hard to control the worry? Or is this the first time you’ve had this kind of ongoing anxiety?

This is definitely the first time I’ve ever experienced this kind of persistent, daily anxiety. Before my promotion about fifteen months ago, I always managed my responsibilities well using planning and organization. This overwhelming, uncontrollable worry only started and became my daily reality after I took on the new role.
If the work promotion and job pressure were completely removed, do you think your anxiety would mostly go away, or would you still have the same constant worry most days?
Honestly, I'm really not sure about that. It's so hard to even imagine my life without this constant job pressure right now, so I haven't really thought about how I would feel without it.
If the job stress were removed, do you think your anxiety would mostly go away within a few months, or do you feel it would keep going at the same level even without that stressor?

I'm honestly not sure if it would completely go away. While work is definitely the main trigger, I find myself constantly worrying about other small things now, so the anxiety might just keep going. It's really hard to say how I would feel without the job pressure.
If the job stress were removed, do you think your anxiety would mostly go away within a few months, or do you feel it would keep going at the same level even without that stressor?

I'm really not sure and I haven't thought about it much, to be honest. This constant stress and worry have just become my normal for so long now that I can't even imagine what it would feel like to not have them.
If the work stress were to end, do you think your anxiety would gradually settle down within a few months, or would it keep going at the same level even without that stressor?

I'm honestly not sure if it would settle down because the work stress has been so constant. I worry my mind might just find other things to worry about, especially since I already find myself stressing over non-work things like whether I locked my apartment door.

The anxiety only started after my promotion about fifteen months ago, so it has been going on for well over six months now. While that situation triggered it, the worry is no longer just tied to work and has spread to everyday things, like obsessively worrying about whether I locked my apartment door.
